sections.heading: A bounded retry succeeds
text: Fictional design walkthrough, not a trace or simulation. Timings, outcomes and policy thresholds are authored examples.
bullets: One idempotent read, at most three attempts, a 1000 ms caller deadline and 200 ms per-attempt timeouts.
Backoff values are selected example jitter samples (60 ms from [0,100], then 120 ms from [0,200]); playback does not draw random delays.
Rows distinguish caller-observed attempts from client backoff. A caller timeout does not prove that server execution stopped.

initial.note: 1000 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

steps.text: t=100 ms. Call 1 returned HTTP 503. The policy admits another read: 60 ms selected backoff + 200 ms timeout fit within the remaining 900 ms.

limits.note: 900 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

safe.detail: Read-only GET; no write is repeated

transient.detail: HTTP 503 is retryable under this example policy

steps.text: t=160 ms. The selected 60 ms backoff finishes. No dependency call occurred during this delay.

limits.note: 840 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

steps.text: t=360 ms. Call 2 reached its 200 ms caller timeout. The remote operation may still be running; this read is safe to repeat. A 120 ms delay plus another 200 ms timeout fit.

limits.note: 640 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

safe.detail: Read-only GET; no write is repeated

transient.detail: Caller timeout is retryable for this read

steps.text: t=480 ms. The selected 120 ms backoff finishes. Only this caller layer owns retries.

limits.note: 520 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

steps.text: t=630 ms. Call 3 succeeds after 150 ms. Return the result with 370 ms left; no fourth attempt is needed or allowed.

limits.note: 370 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

sections.heading: The next attempt cannot fit
text: Fictional design walkthrough, not a trace or simulation. Timings, outcomes and policy thresholds are authored examples.
bullets: Separate scenario: 350 ms attempt timeouts, 1000 ms deadline, at most three attempts.
This example requires the full selected delay plus a full attempt timeout to fit; it does not shorten the final timeout.
No attempt is started merely because the attempt-count limit has room. An elapsed value of 800 ms does not mean the 1000 ms deadline expired.

initial.note: 1000 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

steps.text: t=350 ms. Call 1 times out. This policy requires a full 350 ms timeout after its selected delay; 100 + 350 fits in 650 ms.

limits.note: 650 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

safe.detail: Read-only GET; no write is repeated

steps.text: t=450 ms. The selected 100 ms backoff finishes; the next call can start.

limits.note: 550 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

steps.text: t=800 ms. Call 2 times out. Although the attempt cap allows one more call, the next selected 200 ms delay plus a full 350 ms timeout cannot fit in 200 ms.

limits.note: 200 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

safe.detail: Read-only GET; no write is repeated

steps.text: Return failure at t=800 ms. Do not sleep or send a third call. This is an admission decision before the deadline expires, not an elapsed-time overflow.

limits.note: 200 ms remain before the caller deadline. Example values.

attempts.note: Two calls were sent. Planned backoff 2 and attempt 3 never happened.

sections.heading: Open, reject, probe, recover
text: Fictional design walkthrough, not a trace or simulation. Timings, outcomes and policy thresholds are authored examples.
bullets: One caller-process circuit for one dependency; the guard is a logical component, not another network service.
Example policy: three consecutive dependency failures open the circuit for five seconds; local rejections do not count. One probe is allowed at a time; one success closes and resets the counter.
These are separate caller requests. The timing panel reveals completed intervals, so its extent can lag the clock counter during a delay or probe.

steps.text: t=100 ms. Call 1 fails with HTTP 503. Record one counted failure; the local circuit stays closed. These are separate caller requests, not retries of one request.
t=400 ms. Call 2 fails. Two consecutive counted failures remain below the configured threshold of three.
t=700 ms. Call 3 fails and reaches the threshold. Open this circuit until t=5700 ms. The dependency is not called again during that interval.
t=900 ms. Another caller request is rejected locally. No dependency call or retry occurs, and this rejection does not increment the dependency-failure counter.
t=5700 ms. The open interval ends. Admit one half-open probe; concurrent requests would be rejected while it runs. The probe has not succeeded yet.
t=5800 ms. The probe returns HTTP 200. This example closes after one successful probe and resets its consecutive-failure counter. A failed probe would reopen the circuit.
t=6080 ms. A subsequent normal call succeeds. One local rejection avoided one dependency call during the open interval.
